video_title: Can Aerodrome Become Ethereum’s Dominant Spot Exchange? | Alexander Cutler
gist: Alex Cutler, CEO of Dromos and core contributor to Aerodrome/Velodrome, details the MetaDex03 upgrade that merges Aerodrome and Velodrome into one exchange under a single token and expands it to Ethereum mainnet and Circle's Arc, adding a rev engine (MEV and bridge-fee internalization), a productivity-linked emissions 'air engine', Slipstream v3 and a cross-chain MetaSwaps router. His core thesis is that paying liquidity providers the most — by wrapping 100% of protocol revenue into the locked token — is the only durable moat in onchain spot markets, evidenced by share gains on Optimism and Base, 40–60% of onchain FX volume, and a claimed 70% flow collapse in Uniswap v4's USDC/USDT pool on Base after its fee switch. He sizes spot DEXs as the largest onchain fee vertical outside stablecoins ($5B in fees last year) and argues RWAs, FX and tokenized equities are the next growth verticals.

themes.theme: MetaDex03 upgrade and the Aerodrome–Velodrome merger

insights.claim: Aerodrome and Velodrome are being merged into a single exchange united around a single token as part of the MetaDex03 upgrade, ending the two-protocol/two-token structure that has existed since Velodrome launched on Optimism roughly four years ago.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A single-token merger changes the value-accrual math for both AERO and VELO holders and concentrates all cross-chain revenue into one claim — the key thing to model before the upgrade ships.
insights.quote: not only will aerodrome and drrome be coming together into a single exchange united around a single token

insights.claim: MetaDex03 adds a 'rev engine' that internalizes new revenue streams beyond swap fees — specifically MEV capture and cross-chain bridge fees — and routes them back to the token.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Expands the revenue base a locked-token holder is claiming on, so fee multiples computed on swap fees alone will understate post-upgrade economics.
insights.quote: we have the rev engine which is allowing us to internalize additional revenue streams like me capture u crosschain bridge fees right and direct that value right back to the token

insights.claim: The 'air engine' makes token emissions dynamic and tied to each pool's productivity, lowering the overall emission rate rather than paying a flat schedule to liquidity.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Emissions-per-unit-of-revenue is the core valuation lever for ve(3,3) DEXs; productivity-linked emissions should improve that ratio and reduce sell pressure.
insights.quote: you can just think of it as more value is coming in and less value is coming out of our of our system

insights.claim: Aerodrome claims it has generated more revenue than any other exchange over the past six months, both in absolute terms and relative to emissions paid out.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Revenue relative to emissions is the cleanest efficiency screen for incentive-driven DEXs; if verifiable it makes Aerodrome the benchmark comparison for any competing spot venue.
insights.quote: we have done more revenue in the last uh 6 months than any other uh exchange

insights.claim: MetaDex03 ships a new AMM, Slipstream v3, that supports institutional-grade pools that can plug into external verification/compliance stacks.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Permissioned-but-onchain pools are the technical precondition for regulated RWA and institutional flow to route through a public AMM.

insights.claim: MetaSwaps is being launched as a combined cross-chain swapper, bridge and aggregator in one product that abstracts away bridging, token-on-network selection and even having gas on the destination chain.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: If it works, Aerodrome captures bridge and aggregator fee layers that today accrue to third parties like bridges and DEX aggregators — a direct competitive threat to that category.
insights.quote: the core of which is MetaSwaps which is the first combined crosschain swapper bridge and uh aggregator allin-one product

insights.claim: Cutler frames the ambition explicitly as replicating Hyperliquid's category dominance but for spot rather than derivatives, via maximum value distribution to token holders.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Sets the comparable: investors can benchmark Aerodrome's value-capture-to-token ratio and share trajectory directly against HYPE's.
insights.quote: we very much want to do for spot markets what Hyperlid did you know for uh derivative markets

themes.theme: Chain selection: Base, Circle Arc, Ethereum mainnet

insights.claim: Cutler argues block space is oversupplied and that generalized, undifferentiated L2s will consolidate because activity does not persist once liquidity incentives end.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Bearish for generic L2 token valuations premised on ecosystem incentives; favors chains with a native distribution or asset-issuance edge.
insights.quote: the issue was not lack of block space right the issue is what is that block space being used for

insights.claim: The bet on Base was made because Coinbase's vertical integration turns the chain into a distribution vehicle — Coinbase.com's Bitcoin lending product runs on Morpho on Base, and any token launched on Aerodrome trades instantly on Coinbase.com.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: The Coinbase distribution loop is the actual moat for Base-native protocols; it is a screening criterion for which chains a protocol should deploy on next.
insights.quote: today, any token that launches on a drone trades instantly on Coinbase.com, right? we have access to millions and millions of users

insights.claim: Circle's Arc has a planned mainnet launch on September 16 with Aerodrome named a day-one partner.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: A dated catalyst: Arc's launch is a near-term test of whether Aerodrome's model ports to an institution-focused chain.
insights.quote: yesterday circles arc announced plan mainet launch for September 16th with a drrome named as a day one partner

insights.claim: Arc's differentiation is Circle's ability to onboard institutional partners and RWA issuers for whom even Ethereum is too far out, then act as an EVM-compatible bridge between them and the broader onchain economy.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Arc's value hinges on asset issuance quality, not block space; watch which institutional issuers actually deploy there at launch.

insights.claim: FX is the specific vertical Aerodrome is targeting on Arc, because the binding constraint on scaling onchain FX has been the quality of the tokenized representations of the underlying currencies, which Circle is positioned to fix with issuers.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Better wrapped-currency quality is the unlock for onchain FX volume; track EURC-style pair depth as the leading indicator.
insights.quote: the big issue in scaling FX onchain uh has been the quality of of uh the representations of the underlying assets

insights.claim: Aerodrome already offers better execution on the EURC/USDC pair than Wise, and far better than a bank charging multiple percentage points to convert.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A concrete cost benchmark showing onchain FX can undercut fintech remittance rails — the wedge for payment-rail integrations.
insights.quote: we can give better execution today on Aerad Drrome than you can get on Wise

insights.claim: Cutler dismisses first-mover advantage in DEXs: neither Velodrome on Optimism nor Aerodrome on Base was first, both arrived after Uniswap and Curve were entrenched, and both still took the number one position — which he argues never reverts once achieved.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: The Ethereum mainnet deployment should be underwritten on the LP-payout playbook, not on incumbency, when handicapping share gains against Uniswap.
insights.quote: that is a position that those dexes once they pay them, they never lose

insights.claim: The mainnet playbook is explicitly modeled on the SushiSwap vampire attack, in which simply offering LPs a premium over Uniswap drained 50% of Uniswap's TVL within one week.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Gives a historical magnitude for how fast mercenary TVL can move if Aerodrome's mainnet rewards clear Uniswap's — watch mainnet TVL migration in the weeks post-launch.
insights.quote: all they did was offered LPS a premium to what they could earn on Uniswap and within one week, uh, you know, unis swap had lost 50% of its TPL

themes.theme: LP payout economics as the only moat

insights.claim: Cutler reduces DEX competition to a single variable: liquidity providers are purely mercenary and will move to whichever venue pays the highest reward for the same service, so the highest-paying venue wins share mechanically.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Reduces DEX due diligence to a comparable LP-yield spread across venues — a measurable, trackable metric rather than a narrative.
insights.quote: if you're a liquidity provider and a venue is offering you a dollar and another venue is offering you a buck 50 where are you going to park your liquidity right

insights.claim: Aerodrome pays LPs more than swap fees alone justify because AERO wraps the current and future value of the whole exchange — swap fees plus liquidity incentives plus launch payments — so emitting AERO transfers a claim on that entire bundle.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Explains why AERO can trade at a premium to pure swap-fee multiples, and why the token's value and LP acquisition cost are the same lever.
insights.quote: that collective value isn't just swap fees. Um it's liquidity payments uh or incentives. It's launch payments and and incentives. So it represents a justified sort of premium over swap fees alone.

insights.claim: Locked AERO earns 100% of exchange revenue at any given time, with limits enforced by immutable code and emissions controlled entirely by voters.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Full pass-through with no protocol treasury skim is the differentiator against fee-switch models — the basis for direct yield comparison versus UNI.
insights.quote: you can take Arrow uh lock it and earn 100% of the exchanges revenue um at any given time

insights.claim: Uniswap's fee switch redirects up to 25% of LP fees on v2 and v3 to UNI, which Cutler frames as a structural handicap — Aerodrome only has to beat 75 cents on the dollar.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: The fee switch is a share-loss risk for Uniswap, not just a revenue gain; the trade is long the venue that pays LPs the full dollar.
insights.quote: it's like up to 25% of the fees a liquidity provider is is earning might be redirected back to uh Uniurn. So, uh we can certainly offer you more than 75 cents on the dollar.

insights.claim: Cutler cites data showing that after the Uniswap v4 fee was applied to the USDC/USDT pool on Base, flows through that pool dropped roughly 70% — and therefore fees dropped 70% — with the flow migrating to Aerodrome.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A live empirical case that DEX fee extraction is demand-elastic; a warning sign for revenue models that assume flows are sticky after a fee switch.
insights.quote: this tax that they have put on the flows that are coming in resulted in like a 70% drop off in the amount of flows flowing through that pool which is of course 70% drop off in the fees. And where did those flows go? Right over to Aerodrome.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid is presented as the second proof point of the maximum-distribution thesis, distributing roughly 97% of value captured back to the token and, like Aerodrome, taking no VC funding.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Sets a distribution-ratio benchmark (~97–100%) that competing token models must approach to be defensible.
insights.quote: they distribute I think 97% or so of all the value captured um by the exchange back to the token

insights.claim: Cutler rejects the 'reinvest in growth' argument against full distribution, saying crypto teams historically reinvest in their own lifestyles and exit; Dromos instead funds growth from the revenue its own locked token position earns, giving it the same incentive as any other holder.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Reframes 'team treasury' as a governance risk; the alignment test is whether the team is paid through the same token claim as holders.
insights.quote: I think the history of crypto is they won't they'll reinvest it in growth of maybe their own personal [laughter] life and uh you know slowly exit the stage uh later

insights.claim: Aerodrome does buyback-and-lock rather than buyback-and-burn, on the logic that the token is a claim on revenues passed through in the form they accrue, so locking keeps the position productive.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A distinct tokenomic design worth contrasting against burn-based models when assessing which mechanism actually compounds holder claims.
insights.quote: we're not buying back and burning the token... We do buybacks and locking, but we buy back and lock because the token represents a claim on these revenues

insights.claim: Coinbase Ventures bought AERO on the open market in what Cutler says may still be the largest liquid investment in its history and locked the tokens, giving Coinbase an economic lever over the venue where it would issue onchain products.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Explains the structural reason Coinbase product launches should keep routing to Aerodrome — the issuer captures a cut of the activity it creates.
insights.quote: somebody like Coinbase Ventures who went on the market and they bought uh what was at that point and may still hold the record for their largest liquid investment in their in their history and they locked those tokens

insights.claim: Cutler generalizes maximum value redistribution beyond crypto competition, arguing it is the onchain economy's moat against traditional firms, which capture efficiency gains for insiders rather than passing them through.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A screen for durable onchain business models: any extracted margin invites an undercutter, so high-take-rate onchain businesses are structurally fragile.
insights.quote: every bit of margin that's extracted is is a bounty. It's an opportunity for somebody to come in and give a better offer.

insights.claim: Cutler sizes MEV as hundreds of millions of dollars spent and captured annually across chains, making it a large addressable revenue pool for an AMM that can internalize part of it.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Frames the upside of the rev engine: capturing even a slice of MEV is a material new revenue line relative to current DEX fee bases.
insights.quote: hundreds of millions of dollars are are spent and captured um around [snorts] ME across uh different different chains

insights.claim: Aerodrome's MEV auction works by having its dynamic fee module detect the chain-level priority fee auction and raise pool fees proportionally to how aggressively searchers are bidding to jump the queue, redirecting part of the arbitrage value to LPs.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A replicable mechanism design: any AMM able to read the priority-fee signal can claw MEV back from sequencers, which is a revenue threat to sequencer economics.
insights.quote: what you can do with that dynamic fee module is it can detect um at the chain level that priority fee auction um on the underlying chain

insights.claim: Cutler expects the MEV auction to be roughly neutral for searchers rather than disruptive: on a $100 arbitrage where a searcher bids $10, the total bid stays near $10 but perhaps 20% now goes to the AMM instead of entirely to the sequencer.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Implies the cost is borne by sequencer/L2 revenue, not by searcher participation — so expect little flow loss but a hit to chain-level MEV take.
insights.quote: they'll still probably pay in uh something like $10, but maybe now 20% of it is going over to the AMM and and the rest is going to the sequencer

insights.claim: The second-order effect Cutler expects from MEV redistribution is a reinforcing loop: better-compensated LPs supply deeper liquidity, which creates larger arbitrage opportunities and therefore more MEV to share.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: If the loop holds, MEV capture compounds rather than being a one-time fee bump — the key assumption to test post-launch.

themes.theme: RWAs, FX and tokenized equities as the next spot verticals

insights.claim: Cutler argues low crypto-native trading volumes are a supply problem, not a demand problem — years of low-float high-FDV and extractive issuance means there simply are not many good tokens to trade.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Reframes the bear market: volume recovers with better assets, not with sentiment, so watch issuance quality rather than price for the turn.
insights.quote: I am not surprised that trading volumes on digital assets, you know, are at some of the lowest, you know, they've ever been. Um, and why is that? Well, we don't really have a lot of very good tokens

insights.claim: As of last year's check, roughly 90% of the top 100 tokens redistributed no value at all, and Cutler predicts increasing consolidation into the minority that do — as already happened around HYPE.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A concrete allocation filter: concentrate in the ~10% of tokens with real distribution and expect the rest to lose relative share.
insights.quote: it was still like 90% of the tokens in the top 100 didn't redistribute any value at all

insights.claim: Onchain equities and FX activity is counter-cyclical relative to crypto's four-year cycle, so routing that flow through spot exchanges creates fee revenue that persists through crypto bear markets.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: RWA flow could de-cyclicalize DEX revenue, justifying a higher multiple on venues that dominate those pairs versus purely crypto-native venues.
insights.quote: some of these things are counteryclical, right? uh this is activity that if you bring onchain and it is flowing through spot exchanges um you're seeing a type of activity that won't follow you the four-year cycle

insights.claim: Coinbase's tokenized equities product is close to launch — Cutler cites Jesse Pollak saying it may be weeks away — and he calls it the definitive version, comparable to what Coinbase did with cbBTC applied to equities.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A near-term catalyst for Base-native spot venues; Aerodrome is positioning to be the primary trading venue for those assets at launch.
insights.quote: I think Jesse said yesterday they're very close, maybe weeks away

insights.claim: Aerodrome captures 40–60% of onchain FX volume most weeks and in many weeks this year has done more FX volume than every other DEX on every other chain combined.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: An existing dominant share in a growth vertical — the base case for extending the same position into tokenized stocks.
insights.quote: We are the top venue most most weeks, right? 40 to 60% on onchain FX volume.

insights.claim: Cutler states Aerodrome is the definitive onchain venue for trading Bitcoin, doing more volume than every other DEX on every other chain combined, and wants to replicate that position in tokenized stocks.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Establishes the pattern — dominate the largest single asset in each vertical — which is the metric to track as tokenized equities go live.
insights.quote: just as we are the definitive venue for trading the top digital asset in Bitcoin today. Um, doing more volume than every other DEX, every other chain combined.

insights.claim: Cutler argues you cannot win onchain spot exchange markets without dominating the biggest growth verticals, which he identifies as FX and tokenized equities rather than crypto-native pairs.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Sets the competitive scoreboard for the next cycle: share of RWA/FX pairs, not share of memecoin volume.

themes.theme: AMMs versus prop AMMs and order books

insights.claim: Cutler concedes prop AMMs have found traction on Solana around a handful of blue-chip assets but argues their fatal flaw is that all liquidity on those platforms disappears exactly during black-swan market events, permanently capping their share.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A structural argument for why protocols dependent on reliable pricing and liquidity access cannot build on prop-AMM liquidity — relevant to lending and oracle design.
insights.quote: all the liquidity on those platforms disappears the minute it is absolutely needed

insights.claim: Cutler flags spoofing in prop AMM books as an unresolved issue — aggregators and large takers cannot fully trust quoted prices, and reported volumes may partly reflect misquoted flow that will not sustain.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Treat prop-AMM volume statistics as potentially overstated, and treat scale as a regulatory trigger rather than a validation.
insights.quote: the degree to which they can even trust those books to give the quote that they are promised at any given time and how much of the volumes they are seeing are perhaps based on misqued um uh volumes

insights.claim: Cutler predicts prop AMMs face a regulatory cliff: spoofing is tolerated while they are niche, but once they scale, regulators will scrutinize a centralized product that may not be surfacing real prices.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A latent tail risk for the prop-AMM category that scales with its own success — worth pricing into any exposure to that market-structure bet.
insights.quote: if you know anything about spoofing in traditional markets the moment they are not niche uh that is going to be something that I think regulators are going to take a very very close look at

insights.claim: Cutler reports that an operator of one of the largest prop AMMs across several networks told him Base is the ecosystem where they have struggled most, because Aerodrome rewards LPs at a rate that makes competing for that flow uneconomical.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: First-hand evidence that LP-payout intensity, not technology, is what repels professional market makers — a testable pattern to check on other chains.
insights.quote: Bass is actually the ecosystem where they have struggled most to find any traction

insights.claim: Cutler frames RFQ systems as synergistic rather than competitive with AMMs, since RFQ pricing is ultimately accessed from or balanced against AMM liquidity, while centralized order books continue to lose share to decentralized venues.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Supports treating AMM depth as the base layer of onchain price formation; CEXs adopting permissionless pools is the tell.
insights.quote: centralized exchanges are increasingly shifting to distributing the permissionless pools and permissionless infrastructure of decentralized exchanges

insights.claim: Aerodrome is working to calibrate its dynamic fees to more fully replicate order-book-like execution by pulling prices from centralized venues and redistributing more of that value to LPs.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Dynamic fee sophistication is becoming the competitive frontier in AMM design — it addresses LVR, the main structural cost of passive LPing.

themes.theme: Regulation, token transparency and cycle sentiment

insights.claim: As of the August 7 recording, prediction-market odds on the Clarity Act had fallen to 13%, the day before Senate recess.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: A dated market-implied probability for the main US crypto market-structure bill — the baseline against which post-recess news should be repriced.
insights.quote: Clarity Act odds have fallen down to uh 13% as of this morning

insights.claim: Cutler says developer protections are the single most important Clarity Act provision for Dromos, citing years of legal exposure building as a doxxed American DeFi founder from 2022 with no revenue to fund a defense, and the resulting brain drain of builders out of the US.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific bill provision whose survival matters most to US-domiciled DeFi teams, independent of whether the bill passes this year.

insights.claim: Cutler endorses Brian Armstrong's 'no bill is better than a bad bill' position, arguing FTX-era draft legislation would have been destructive to DeFi and good for centralized incumbents.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Failure of the Clarity Act is not automatically bearish DeFi; the content of the bill matters more than its passage.
insights.quote: when Brian Armstrong came out and said, "No bill is better than a bad bill." I agree.

insights.claim: Cutler expects Clarity-style legislation to eventually pass even if not before year-end, comparing it to the stablecoin bill that was declared dead before passing at the last line, and notes regulators at all levels are currently friendly with banks now building on crypto rather than fighting it.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Argues regulatory outcome risk is largely priced out regardless of the legislative calendar — timing, not direction, is the open question.
insights.quote: we've got regulators, uh, you know, at all levels right now that are incredibly friendly to the industry. This industry is not going anywhere.

insights.claim: Aerodrome's token profile has no team-allocated liquid vesting tokens, no tokens sold to third parties, and no paid marketing, influencer or exchange-listing spend, with all wallets trackable onchain and supply limits enforced by immutable code.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A concrete disclosure checklist to compare AERO against other tokens' unlock and insider-supply overhangs.
insights.quote: there are no team allocated uh liquid vesting tokens, right? Um there are no tokens that we've sold to third parties. Uh we don't pay for marketing or influencers or um exchange listings.

insights.claim: Aerodrome's Ignition product lets projects skip the traditional exchange listing process, which Cutler says is typically extractive and takes about 10% of a token's supply, and instead auction and build liquidity onchain to veAERO voters.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Quantifies the cost of the incumbent listing channel (~10% of supply) that onchain launch venues are undercutting — the wedge for DEX-native issuance.
insights.quote: the traditional like exchange listing process that is usually very extractive takes 10% of the supply

insights.claim: Nearly every project that has launched via Ignition has also completed the Token Transparency Framework report, so veAERO voters can review unlocks, investors and commitments before allocating in the initial auction.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Disclosure at the launch venue lowers the required discount rate for new issues — a structural improvement in onchain primary-market quality.

insights.claim: Cutler says he personally excludes from consideration any token that has not participated in a transparency framework, and argues coordinated paid-shill campaigns are identifiable because organic theses build gradually while paid ones appear across every large account in a single week.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: A practical screen for detecting manufactured narratives before entering a position.
insights.quote: I instantly just remove from the list anybody who hasn't participated in something like this

insights.claim: Cutler's core advice to builders and allocators is that crypto Twitter is a lagging signal, not a leading one — the divergence is visible at institutional conferences where banks and issuers are hiring aggressively and have no idea sentiment is poor.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Argues for weighting institutional pipeline evidence over social sentiment when timing exposure in a drawdown.
insights.quote: you need to treat crypto Twitter as a lagging signal, not a leading signal

insights.claim: Cutler cites Brian Armstrong's bet that 10% of global GDP comes onchain within five years, mostly invisibly, as the institutional base case driving current hiring and product migration.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: The TAM anchor institutions are underwriting; if directionally right, infrastructure fee pools scale far beyond current crypto-native volumes.
insights.quote: in the next 5 years 10% of 10% of global GDP comes on chain

insights.claim: Cutler predicts the easy-money era of uncorrelated liquidity pools paying 8,000% APR and alpha-group exit liquidity is ending, and that onchain asset evaluation will increasingly resemble traditional markets — disappointing a loud cohort of crypto Twitter participants.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: Implies a rotation toward fundamentals-based token selection; venues and assets built for that regime gain share as speculative rotation flow fades.
insights.quote: you could buy you know the worst the worst tokens, pair them in a liquidity pool uncorrelated, earn 8,000% APR while they're both 10xing at the same time

insights.claim: Cutler sizes spot exchanges as the highest-value vertical of the onchain economy outside stablecoins at $5 billion in fees last year, versus roughly $3 billion for derivatives, about $2 billion for chains, and $1–2 billion for lending.
insights.speaker: Alexander Cutler
insights.so_what: The clearest fee-pool ranking in the episode — it justifies concentrating exposure in spot DEX equity-like tokens over lending or L1/L2 tokens.
insights.quote: spot exchanges did $5 billion in fees last year. Um you know derivatives did about three billion lending you know I think or chains did like two something like that lending did one to two something like that.
